sentences.en: That research focused on boys from some of the poorest, toughest areas of the city.
sentences.zh: 那项研究的重点是来自该市最贫困、最艰难地区的男孩。

sentences.en: Together, these studies provide a vivid picture of men's health over the course of their lives.
sentences.zh: 这些研究共同生动地展现了男性一生中的健康状况。

sentences.en: Now, you could say this research is obviously incomplete because it leaves out more than half the population.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会说这项研究显然是不完整的，因为它遗漏了半数以上的人口。

sentences.en: But it does tell a striking story about a phenomenon that has many researchers worried.
sentences.zh: 但它确实讲述了一个引人注目的故事，关于一个让许多研究人员担忧的现象。

sentences.en: Social isolation among men.
sentences.zh: 男性的社会孤立。

sentences.en: I really don't think I dealt with it.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为我没有去处理它。

sentences.en: I think I viewed it as sort of a circumstance rather than a problem.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我把它看作是一种状况，而不是一个问题。

sentences.en: But there was also a part of me that realized I was alone.
sentences.zh: 但我的内心深处也意识到我是孤身一人。

sentences.en: When we come back, we look at the profound loneliness of American men.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将关注美国男性的深刻孤独。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: In recent decades, there have been pervasive worries that Americans are spending less time with one another
sentences.zh: 近几十年来，人们普遍担忧美国人花在彼此陪伴上的时间越来越少，

sentences.en: and that the ties that once bound communities together have started to fray.
sentences.zh: 曾经将社区凝聚在一起的纽带已经开始磨损。

sentences.en: Back in 2000, the political scientist Robert Putnam wrote about this idea in his book, Bowling Alone.
sentences.zh: 早在2000年，政治学家罗伯特·帕特南就在他的著作《独自打保龄》中写到了这个观点。

sentences.en: He described how many Americans were opting out of the civic and community organizations that their parents once joined.
sentences.zh: 他描述了许多美国人如何选择退出他们父母曾经加入的公民和社区组织。

sentences.en: More recently, researchers have watched with growing concern as many of us spend increasing amounts of time hunched over our phones
sentences.zh: 最近，研究人员怀着日益增长的担忧观察到，我们许多人花越来越多的时间低头看着手机，

sentences.en: while ignoring those sitting across from us.
sentences.zh: 却忽视了坐在我们对面的人。

sentences.en: There's another form of social isolation that's less talked about, one that disproportionately affects men.
sentences.zh: 还有另一种较少被谈论的社会孤立形式，它对男性的影响尤为严重。

sentences.en: Men like Paul Kugelman.
sentences.zh: 像保罗·库格尔曼这样的男性。

sentences.en: When Paul was a kid growing up in Union City, New Jersey, his parents had a simple rule.
sentences.zh: 保罗小时候在新泽西州联合市长大时，他的父母有一条简单的规则。

sentences.en: Go outside and play and come home when the streetlights come on.
sentences.zh: 出去玩，路灯亮了就回家。

sentences.en: Each weekday, Paul walked to and from school with other kids in his neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 每个工作日，保罗都会和邻里其他孩子一起步行上学放学。

sentences.en: Dawn and George and Joanne and Henry, John.
sentences.zh: 道恩、乔治、琼、亨利、约翰。

sentences.en: When the kids got home, they dropped off their books and ran outside to play.
sentences.zh: 孩子们回到家后，放下书本就跑出去玩。

sentences.en: We'd do whatever.
sentences.zh: 我们会随便玩什么。

sentences.en: It was a tag, ring of Levio, capture the flag, football, whatever.
sentences.zh: 那是抓人游戏、捉迷藏、夺旗、橄榄球，随便什么都行。

sentences.en: It was just, it was friendship.
sentences.zh: 那只是，那是友谊。

sentences.en: You had people you could talk to.
sentences.zh: 你有可以说话的人。

sentences.en: You were part of a community of your peers.
sentences.zh: 你是同龄人社区的一部分。

sentences.en: It was nice.
sentences.zh: 这很好。

sentences.en: It was all so easy.
sentences.zh: 一切都是那么容易。

sentences.en: Paul played pickup football in the vacant lot across the street from his home.
sentences.zh: 保罗在他家街对面空地上玩即兴橄榄球。

sentences.en: He ran into his Aunt Marie at the library.
sentences.zh: 他在图书馆遇到了他的玛丽阿姨。

sentences.en: You'd just run into people all the time when you kind of knew everybody in the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 当你在邻里中基本上认识所有人时，你总是会遇到各种各样的人。

sentences.en: Then, when Paul was nine, he and his family moved 500 miles south to Martinsville, Virginia.
sentences.zh: 后来，保罗九岁时，他和家人向南搬了500英里，来到了弗吉尼亚州马丁斯维尔。

sentences.en: Rural Virginia didn't have all the amenities he was used to in New Jersey,
sentences.zh: 乡下的弗吉尼亚没有他在新泽西习惯的各种便利设施，

sentences.en: like the black and white cookies and coffee cake he used to get at an iconic bakery.
sentences.zh: 比如他以前常在一家标志性面包店买的黑白饼干和咖啡蛋糕。

sentences.en: Not only was there no such thing as Entenmann's, it was like, what do you mean by bagel?
sentences.zh: 不仅没有恩滕曼品牌那样的糕点，而且大家会问，贝果是什么意思？

sentences.en: Paul missed his comfort foods, but that wasn't the only thing that gave him culture shock.
sentences.zh: 保罗想念他习惯的美食，但这并不是唯一让他感到文化冲击的事情。

sentences.en: It was my first few days in school, and the teacher had a thick southern accent,
sentences.zh: 那是我在学校的前几天，老师有着浓重的南方口音，

sentences.en: and she was giving a spelling teSt.
sentences.zh: 她正在进行拼写测验。

sentences.en: What I heard was Alpo, but she said apple.
sentences.zh: 我听到的是阿尔波（Alpo），但她说的是苹果（apple）。

sentences.en: But I heard Alpo, so I wrote Alpo, and these people concluded that I was a screaming idiot
sentences.zh: 但我听成是阿尔波，所以我写了阿尔波，这些人断定我是个尖叫的笨蛋，

sentences.en: because I didn't understand how to spell apple, and I was supposed to be this great student.
sentences.zh: 因为我不知道怎么拼写苹果，而我本该是个绝顶聪明的学生。

sentences.en: So, and it kind of went downhill from there for a while.
sentences.zh: 所以，有一段时间事情就有点急转直下了。

sentences.en: Paul's father was frequently relocated for work,
sentences.zh: 保罗的父亲经常因为工作而搬迁，

sentences.en: after Virginia to Delaware, then South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 继弗吉尼亚之后去了特拉华州，然后是南卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: Each time the family moved, Paul had to navigate a new school and a new social world.
sentences.zh: 每次搬家，保罗都必须适应一所新学校和一个新的社交世界。

sentences.en: Even though he didn't realize it at the time,
sentences.zh: 尽管他当时并没有意识到，

sentences.en: he was gradually developing a strategy to cope with all the moves.
sentences.zh: 他正在逐渐形成一种策略来应对所有的搬迁。

sentences.en: I didn't really interact a whole lot with folks,
sentences.zh: 我其实并没有和大家进行太多的互动，

sentences.en: because it just was like, we're going to move again, so I didn't want the pain, I guess.
sentences.zh: 因为这就像是，我们又要搬家了，所以我猜我不想承受痛苦。

sentences.en: Paul eventually went off to study at the Citadel, a military college in South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 保罗最终去南卡罗来纳州的军事学院——城堡军校学习。

sentences.en: When he arrived, he was told that his classmates would become lifelong friends.
sentences.zh: 当他到达时，有人告诉他，他的同学将成为终身的朋友。

sentences.en: But after they graduated, Paul found his former classmates were not very eager to stay in touch.
sentences.zh: 但毕业后，保罗发现他的前同窗们并不是很热衷于保持联系。

sentences.en: Paul's life took its own trajectory.
sentences.zh: 保罗的人生走上了自己的轨迹。

sentences.en: He got married, had a child, he got divorced.
sentences.zh: 他结婚了，有了孩子，又离婚了。

sentences.en: In his 30s, Paul went to law school and remarried.
sentences.zh: 三十多岁时，保罗读了法学院并再次结婚。

sentences.en: Just like before, he made acquaintances, but...
sentences.zh: 就像以前一样，他结识了一些人，但是……

sentences.en: I was in this place where, in my mind, everything was kind of transient.
sentences.zh: 我身处这样一个地方：在我的脑海里，一切都有点短暂。

sentences.en: He didn't quite realize it, but his social world was shrinking.
sentences.zh: 他并没有完全意识到，但他的社交世界正在萎缩。

sentences.en: The acquaintances he made stayed acquaintances.
sentences.zh: 他结识的人依然只是泛泛之交。

sentences.en: He didn't have the time to develop these into real friendships.
sentences.zh: 他没有时间将这些发展成真正的友谊。

sentences.en: Family and work felt all-consuming.
sentences.zh: 家庭和工作让人感觉精疲力竭。

sentences.en: In his mid-40s, Paul's second marriage fell apart.
sentences.zh: 在他四十岁出头时，保罗的第二段婚姻破裂了。

sentences.en: His ex-wife took the kids and moved several hours away.
sentences.zh: 他的前妻带着孩子搬到了几个小时车程外的地方。

sentences.en: His mother had died young, and Paul was estranged from his father.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲很年轻就去世了，保罗与父亲关系疏远。

sentences.en: He talked to his daughter every day, but that routine ended too.
sentences.zh: 他每天都和女儿通话，但这种日常也结束了。

sentences.en: Even though he was doing meaningful work as a lawyer, it wasn't enough.
sentences.zh: 尽管他作为一名律师在从事有意义的工作，但这还不够。

sentences.en: I guess lonely is the right word.
sentences.zh: 我猜孤独是正确的词。

sentences.en: It was a very lonely time.
sentences.zh: 那是一段非常孤独的时期。

sentences.en: I don't remember specific triggers.
sentences.zh: 我不记得有什么具体的导火索。

sentences.en: It was just this sense of absolute isolation.
sentences.zh: 只有这种绝对孤立的感觉。

sentences.en: Absolute's too strong a word.
sentences.zh: 绝对这个词太绝对了。

sentences.en: Because I did go to work, and I did have interactions at work.
sentences.zh: 因为我确实去上班了，而且我在工作中确实有互动。

sentences.en: And I cherished those.
sentences.zh: 我很珍惜这些。

sentences.en: But, you know, at the end of the day, it was just me.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，到头来，只有我一个人。

sentences.en: He drank heavily for a while.
sentences.zh: 他有一段时间酗酒得很厉害。

sentences.en: Then he got into exercise.
sentences.zh: 后来他开始健身。

sentences.en: He eventually completed an Ironman triathlon.
sentences.zh: 他最终完成了铁人三项比赛。

sentences.en: But these distractions couldn't quite stamp out the fact that he was desperate for friendship, for connection.
sentences.zh: 但这些消遣无法完全消除这样一个事实：他极度渴望友谊，渴望联结。

sentences.en: So desperate that he turned to an inanimate object for comfort.
sentences.zh: 极度渴望到他向一个无生命的物体寻求慰藉。

sentences.en: I was in my apartment, and one of the fixtures in the apartment was a post that runs floor to ceiling, and a banister runs out of that.
sentences.zh: 我在我的公寓里，公寓里的固定设施之一是一根从地板通到天花板的柱子，一根扶手从那里延伸出来。

sentences.en: And the post became my friend.
sentences.zh: 然后这根柱子成了我的朋友。

sentences.en: I would hug the poSt.
sentences.zh: 我会拥抱这根柱子。

sentences.en: I would hug the post for all it was worth, because I was getting some kind of feedback physically.
sentences.zh: 我会死死地拥抱这根柱子，因为我在身体上得到了一些反馈。

sentences.en: It was at that point I realized, I have got to do something, because when you get to the place where you need to hug a post to feel something that you need,
sentences.zh: 正是在那时我意识到，我必须做点什么，因为当你沦落到需要拥抱一根柱子来感受你所需要的东西时，

sentences.en: if that's not a wake-up call, nothing is.
sentences.zh: 如果这还算不上警钟，那就没什么算得上了。

sentences.en: Paul's childhood offered a model of a close-knit community.
sentences.zh: 保罗的童年提供了一个紧密团结的社区的模范。

sentences.en: His life in his 40s was nothing like that model.
sentences.zh: 他四十多岁的生活与那种模范毫无相似之处。

sentences.en: Looking back, Paul says he ignored the warning signs that his social world was shrinking.
sentences.zh: 回首往事，保罗说他忽视了社交世界正在萎缩的警告信号。

sentences.en: I really don't think I dealt with it, candidly.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，我真的认为我没有去面对它。

sentences.en: I think I viewed it as sort of a circumstance rather than a problem.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我把它看作是一种状况，而不是一个问题。

sentences.en: It's kind of like gravity.
sentences.zh: 这有点像重力。

sentences.en: But there was also a part of me that realized I was alone.
sentences.zh: 但我的内心深处也意识到我是孤身一人。

sentences.en: Even when Paul got the courage to reach out to other people, he found himself butting up against social rules.
sentences.zh: 甚至当保罗鼓起勇气去接触其他人时，他发现自己遇到了社会规则的阻碍。

sentences.en: He went to introduce himself to neighbors in his apartment building, but found them more bewildered than friendly.
sentences.zh: 他去公寓楼里向邻居做自我介绍，却发现对方与其说友好，不如说感到困惑。

sentences.en: It's not like anything they said in particular.
sentences.zh: 倒不是他们说的具体内容。

sentences.en: It's kind of the look, the countenance.
sentences.zh: 有点像那个眼神，那个神态。

sentences.en: It's like, you're an odd dude.
sentences.zh: 就好像在说，你是个奇怪的家伙。

sentences.en: Why is a 51-year-old guy knocking on our door to tell us he lives next door?
sentences.zh: 为什么一个51岁的家伙要敲我们的门来告诉我们他住在隔壁？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: Part of it is I think there's a stigma to being viewed as being alone or lonely.
sentences.zh: 部分原因我认为被视为孤单或孤独是带有某种耻辱感的。

sentences.en: The irony was Paul himself wasn't very forgiving to people who were in the same boat that he was.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，保罗本人对处境与他相同的人并不那么宽容。

sentences.en: It's funny, like when I got out into the dating realm again, you know, I'm this middle-aged alone person, but I'm very wary of people who are in the same group as I am because,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，比如当我再次涉足约会领域时，你知道，我是个中年单身汉，但我非常警惕那些和我属于同一群体的人，因为，

sentences.en: you know, what are you doing at this age alone?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你这么大年纪了单身在干什么？

sentences.en: Over and over, Paul was reminded that it was hard for a middle-aged man to form meaningful new friendships.
sentences.zh: 保罗一次又一次地被提醒，中年男子很难建立有意义的新友谊。

sentences.en: After he started dating, he noticed how his girlfriend, Kim, easily struck up conversations and made new connections.
sentences.zh: 开始约会后，他注意到他的女友金是如何轻而易举地打开话匣子并建立新的联系的。

sentences.en: She can make friends anywhere she goes, and nobody bats an eye about a woman going up and just chatting either a guy or girl up.
sentences.zh: 她无论走到哪里都能交到朋友，而且无论女人上去跟男人还是女人聊天，都没人会大惊小怪。

sentences.en: It wasn't just Kim.
sentences.zh: 不只是金。

sentences.en: It felt like there was a difference between men and women.
sentences.zh: 感觉男人和女人之间确实存在差异。

sentences.en: At one point, they were at a festival.
sentences.zh: 有一次，他们在一个节日上。

sentences.en: Seemingly out of nowhere, Kim's friend, Polly, gathered together seven or eight people to hang out.
sentences.zh: 仿佛凭空出现一般，金的朋友波莉召集了七八个人一起闲逛。

sentences.en: And I had this feeling if I tried to do that, it would be like, okay, who's the creepy old dude, you know?
sentences.zh: 而我有一种感觉，如果我试图那样做，大家会觉得，好吧，这个令人毛骨悚然的老家伙是谁啊？

sentences.en: But I think there is a stigma for guys, and I don't know if it's just a, you know, a self-imposed thing or actually society views it that way.
sentences.zh: 但我认为对男人来说确实存在一种耻辱感，我不知道这只是一种自我强加的东西，还是社会确实是这么看的。

sentences.en: From my experience, I think society views it that way, but I can't say for sure.
sentences.zh: 根据我的经验，我认为社会是这么看的，但我无法百分之百确定。

sentences.en: He now recognizes that even though it's hard, reaching out to other people is essential.
sentences.zh: 他现在认识到，尽管很难，但向他人伸出援手是至关重要的。

sentences.en: A rejection of the extension of an offer of friendship or acquaintancehood isn't a rejection.
sentences.zh: 拒绝建立友谊或泛泛之交的延伸并不是一种拒绝。

sentences.en: It's just that that person's not ready.
sentences.zh: 只是那个人还没准备好。

sentences.en: Paul's story is echoed by many other men who reached out to us in recent months.
sentences.zh: 保罗的故事得到了近几个月来联系我们的许多其他男性的共鸣。

sentences.en: Although each story is different in the details, the same themes run through many of them.
sentences.zh: 尽管每个故事的细节各不相同，但许多故事都贯穿着相同的主题。

sentences.en: These men felt they didn't have enough friends.
sentences.zh: 这些男性觉得自己没有足够的朋友。

sentences.en: Even when they wanted to make new friends, they didn't know how to do it.
sentences.zh: 即使他们想结交新朋友，他们也不知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: I really look back on the last 50 such and dearth.
sentences.zh: 我真的回顾了过去50年的这种匮乏。

sentences.en: I am married, and when my wife and I are together, there are things to do and not enough time in the day to do them with our friends.
sentences.zh: 我结婚了，当我和妻子在一起时，有很多事情要做，一天的时间根本不够和我们的朋友们一起完成。

sentences.en: When she and I are apart for more than a day or two, I turn into a hermit.
sentences.zh: 当她和我分开一天或两天以上时，我就变成了一个隐士。

sentences.en: Many married men reported that their wives organized their social activities.
sentences.zh: 许多已婚男性报告说，他们的妻子组织了他们的社交活动。

sentences.en: In a recent episode of Hidden Brain, psychologist Eli Finkel explained how such over-reliance on one person is a new phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 在最近一期《隐藏的大脑》中，心理学家伊利·芬克尔解释了这种对一个人的过度依赖是如何成为一种新现象的。

sentences.en: There was a time not long ago in the United States when people didn't expect their spouse to be partner and lover and best friend combined.
sentences.zh: 在美国不久前曾有过这样一个时期，人们并不期望他们的配偶集伴侣、爱人和挚友于一身。

sentences.en: Marriage for a long time served a set and relatively limited array of different functions for us.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，婚姻对我们而言起到了一组相对有限的不同功能。

sentences.en: And over time, we've piled more and more of these emotional and psychological functions.
sentences.zh: 而随着时间的推移，我们把越来越多的这些情感和心理功能堆积在了一起。

sentences.en: So instead of turning to our close friends and other relatives for nights out on the town, for deep intimate disclosure,
sentences.zh: 因此，相比于去找密友和其他亲戚深夜畅谈、敞开心扉倾诉隐私，

sentences.en: to a larger and larger extent, our spouse has replaced a lot of what we used to look to our broader social network to help us do.
sentences.zh: 在越来越大的程度上，伴侣已经取代了许多我们过去需要依靠更广泛的社交网络来做的事情。

sentences.en: If many men in heterosexual relationships count on wives to be their sole providers of social connection,
sentences.zh: 如果许多异性恋关系中的男性指望妻子成为他们唯一的社交纽带来源，

sentences.en: this places enormous pressure on women in those relationships too.
sentences.zh: 这也给这些关系中的女性带来了巨大的压力。

sentences.en: To be sure, there are exceptions to all of this.
sentences.zh: 当然，凡事都有例外。

sentences.en: But overall, researchers are worried about increasing social isolation among men and where this might lead.
sentences.zh: 但总体而言，研究人员对男性的社会孤立感不断加剧及其可能导致的后果感到担忧。

sentences.en: Some men cope not by running an Ironman or drinking or hugging an inanimate object.
sentences.zh: 有些男性的应对方式不是去跑铁人三项、酗酒或拥抱无生命的物体。

sentences.en: They take more drastic measures.
sentences.zh: 他们采取了更极端的措施。

sentences.en: I spoke to Julie Phillips about this.
sentences.zh: 我为此采访了朱莉·菲利普斯。

sentences.en: She's a sociology professor at Rutgers University.
sentences.zh: 她是罗格斯大学的社会学教授。

sentences.en: Which figure are you looking at here?
sentences.zh: 你在这里看的是哪个图表？

sentences.en: I'll say figure two.
sentences.zh: 我来说图二。

sentences.en: She walked me through a couple of graphs that show the rate of suicide among men of different age groups.
sentences.zh: 她带我看了几张图表，展示了不同年龄段男性的自杀率。

sentences.en: Those rates vary widely from the young to the very old.
sentences.zh: 这些比率从年轻人到老年人各不相同。

sentences.en: Increasingly, however, middle-aged men appear to be at growing risk.
sentences.zh: 然而，中年男性的风险似乎在不断增加。

sentences.en: We saw a fairly sharp increase in suicide rates among men beginning in 1999.
sentences.zh: 我们看到从 1999 年开始，男性的自杀率出现了相当急剧的上升。

sentences.en: So, for example, among men aged 50 to 54, we saw an increase of almost 50% in their suicide rate.
sentences.zh: 因此，例如，在 50 至 54 岁的男性中，我们看到他们的自杀率增加了近 50%。

sentences.en: The increase in the suicide rate among middle-aged men is troubling.
sentences.zh: 中年男性自杀率的上升令人担忧。

sentences.en: It's also a reversal of historical patterns.
sentences.zh: 这也是对历史规律的一种逆转。

sentences.en: Compared to earlier generations, the uptick in suicide seems to be starting earlier and earlier,
sentences.zh: 与早期几代人相比，自杀率的上升似乎开始得越来越早，

sentences.en: especially for men.
sentences.zh: 尤其是对男性而言。

sentences.en: One common interpretation of this trend is that it's driven by economic probleMs.
sentences.zh: 对这一趋势的一种常见解释是，它是受经济问题驱动的。

sentences.en: Julie thinks it's more complicated.
sentences.zh: 朱莉认为情况要复杂得多。

sentences.en: The trend of rising suicide rates among middle-aged men began in the late 1990s,
sentences.zh: 中年男性自杀率上升的趋势始于上世纪 90 年代末，

sentences.en: well before the Great Recession that started in 2007.
sentences.zh: 远在 2007 年爆发的大衰退之前。

sentences.en: Actually, from 1999 to 2005, the increases among the middle-aged were really confined to those boomers
sentences.zh: 事实上，从 1999 年到 2005 年，中年人群的增长实际上仅限于那些

sentences.en: who did not have a college education.
sentences.zh: 没有受过大学教育的婴儿潮一代。

sentences.en: But since 2005, it has now broadened out.
sentences.zh: 但自 2005 年以来，这种现象现在已经扩大了。

sentences.en: It's really been across the board.
sentences.zh: 它实际上已经波及各个群体。

sentences.en: We don't see these differences by education.
sentences.zh: 我们没有看到这种因教育程度而异的差异。

sentences.en: Julie has other ideas about what might be driving these changes.
sentences.zh: 对于究竟是什么在推动这些变化，朱莉有其他的看法。

sentences.en: People have fewer social supports.
sentences.zh: 人们的社会支持减少了。

sentences.en: They're more likely to live far away from family.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能远离家人居住。

sentences.en: Many are opting out of marriage.
sentences.zh: 许多人选择不结婚。

sentences.en: Many are getting divorced.
sentences.zh: 许多人正在离婚。

sentences.en: Even when we choose to connect with others, we're often not doing it in person.
sentences.zh: 即使我们选择与他人联系，也往往不是通过面对面的方式。

sentences.en: I also wonder, too, just about the ways in which we interact
sentences.zh: 我也在想，关于我们的互动方式

sentences.en: and how that has changed, certainly over the past 15, 20 years or so.
sentences.zh: 以及这在过去 15、20 年左右是如何发生变化的。

sentences.en: I mean, the rise of social media, less face-to-face contact.
sentences.zh: 我是说，社交媒体的兴起，面对面的接触减少了。

sentences.en: You know, our entertainment has sort of become more private.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们的娱乐变得更加私密了。

sentences.en: You know, we watch a movie at home rather than going to a theater, for example.
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如我们在家看电影，而不是去电影院。

sentences.en: So, you know, that may also be having, it may be contributing to feelings of isolation,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这可能也带来了影响，它可能会加剧孤立感，

sentences.en: social isolation that could also be producing some of these rising rates.
sentences.zh: 这种社会孤立感也可能是导致这些上升比率的原因之一。

sentences.en: Again, the toll of social isolation isn't just emotional.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，社会孤立的代价不仅仅是情感上的。

sentences.en: An analysis of nearly 150 studies has found that people with strong social relationships
sentences.zh: 对近 150 项研究的分析发现，拥有牢固社会关系的人

sentences.en: had about a 50% lower mortality risk than those with weaker ties.
sentences.zh: 其死亡风险比社交纽带较弱的人低约 50%。

sentences.en: Julianne Holt-Lunstad and her co-authors concluded
sentences.zh: 朱莉安·霍尔特-伦stad 和她的合著者得出结论，

sentences.en: that those with weaker social relationships had a greater risk of death
sentences.zh: 社会关系较弱的人面临的死亡风险更大，

sentences.en: than people who were physically inactive or obese.
sentences.zh: 甚至超过了缺乏身体活动或肥胖的人。

sentences.en: Let me put that another way.
sentences.zh: 换句话说。

sentences.en: Spending time building and nurturing your friendships
sentences.zh: 花时间建立和培养你的友谊

sentences.en: might be just as important to your health as eating right and exercising.
sentences.zh: 对健康的重要性可能不亚于合理饮食和锻炼。

sentences.en: When we come back, we look at the cultural roots of this problem.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将探讨这个问题的文化根源。

sentences.en: These are, you know, human beings with unbelievable emotional and social capacity,
sentences.zh: 这些，你知道，是具有令人难以置信的情感和社会能力的人类，

sentences.en: and we as a culture just completely try to zip it out of them, and we ignore it.
sentences.zh: 而我们作为一个文化群体，却完全试图将这一点从他们身上抹杀掉，并且无视它。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: We're exploring the effects of social isolation over the course of our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们正在探讨社会孤立贯穿我们一生的影响。

sentences.en: In particular, we're looking at men who tend to have a harder time than women
sentences.zh: 特别是，我们正在关注那些与女性相比，

sentences.en: when it comes to making and maintaining friendships.
sentences.zh: 在建立和维持友谊方面往往更显艰难的男性。

sentences.en: Economic forces certainly play a role in eroding social ties,
sentences.zh: 经济力量确实在侵蚀社会纽带方面发挥了作用，

sentences.en: but psychologist Niobe Way thinks that the roots of loneliness among men go deeper.
sentences.zh: 但心理学家尼奥比·韦认为，男性孤独的根源更加深远。

sentences.en: She thinks they are primarily cultural, embedded, and twisted ideas of what it takes to be a man.
sentences.zh: 她认为它们主要是文化上的，根植于并扭曲了对“如何成为一个真正的男人”的看法。

sentences.en: In the late 1980s, Niobe worked as a counselor at a high school in Boston.
sentences.zh: 在 20 世纪 80 年代末，尼奥比曾在波士顿的一所高中担任辅导员。

sentences.en: She expected the boys in her school to talk about their classes,
sentences.zh: 她原本预期学校里的男孩们会谈论他们的课程、

sentences.en: difficulties with family, violence in the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 家庭困难以及社区暴力。

sentences.en: What they were mostly talking about is their friendships
sentences.zh: 而他们主要谈论的是他们的友谊，

sentences.en: and trying to find good friendships and feeling hurt by other boys in the school.
sentences.zh: 试图找到好的友谊，并为学校里其他男孩的伤害感到难过。

sentences.en: At first, she was surprised.
sentences.zh: 起初，她感到很惊讶。

sentences.en: When I started to hear boys, it was at first wondering why they weren't sounding like the boys
sentences.zh: 当我开始听到男孩们说话时，一开始我很纳闷，为什么他们听起来不像我

sentences.en: I thought they were going to sound like.
sentences.zh: 以为他们应该听起来的那样。

sentences.en: And so essentially, it was why didn't they sound like the stereotypes that I had of them,
sentences.zh: 所以本质上是，为什么他们听起来不符合我对他们的刻板印象，

sentences.en: whether as boys or as working class boys or as boys of color, etc.
sentences.zh: 无论是作为男孩、工人阶级男孩还是有色人种男孩等等。

sentences.en: I was thinking they were talking a lot about, you know, friendships.
sentences.zh: 我以为他们会谈论很多关于，你知道的，友谊的事情。

sentences.en: They sounded like, quote unquote, in my head in the late 80s, like girls.
sentences.zh: 在 80 年代末的我脑海里，他们听起来就像所谓的“女孩”。

sentences.en: She wanted to know what was wrong with the boys,
sentences.zh: 她想知道的是男孩们出了什么问题，

sentences.en: not what was wrong with the stereotype.
sentences.zh: 而不是刻板印象出了什么问题。

sentences.en: That's how stereotypes work.
sentences.zh: 这就是刻板印象的作用方式。

sentences.en: We know that they're not true for ourselves, but we somehow think they're true for other people.
sentences.zh: 我们知道它们对我们自己不适用，但我们不知何故认为它们对其他人适用。

sentences.en: As Niobe studied the issue, she discovered that men in other cultures and American men in other times
sentences.zh: 正如尼奥比研究所的那样，她发现其他文化中的男性以及其他时期的美国男性

sentences.en: had no problem developing close, intimate friendships well into adulthood.
sentences.zh: 在成年后发展亲密友谊方面根本没有任何问题。

sentences.en: And the men she knew, at least at one point in their lives, had no problem being deeply and openly emotional.
sentences.zh: 她认识的那些男性，至少在他们生命中的某个时刻，在深刻而公开地表达情感方面也没有任何问题。

sentences.en: I actually had very, very clear memories of my brothers having similar kinds of friendships.
sentences.zh: 其实我有着非常非常清晰的记忆，我的兄弟们也有过类似的友谊。

sentences.en: Niobe remembers a time when she was sitting upstairs in her parents' house and she could hear her younger brother and his friends outside.
sentences.zh: 尼奥比记得有一次她坐在父母家的楼上，能听到她弟弟和他的朋友们在外面。

sentences.en: He was out in the backyard talking with his basketball teammates.
sentences.zh: 他在后院和他的篮球队友聊天。

sentences.en: One of the guys had said something mean to one of the other guys in the group.
sentences.zh: 其中一个家伙对组里的另一个家伙说了句刻薄的话。

sentences.en: And the four of them were processing their feelings around this mean behavior by one of the boys towards the other boys.
sentences.zh: 他们四个人正在消化彼此对其中一个男孩对另一个男孩这种刻薄行为的情绪。

sentences.en: And these were four tough-looking basketball players, athletic, cool kids in the high school.
sentences.zh: 而这四个人看起来都是硬汉篮球运动员，热爱运动，是高中里很酷的孩子。

sentences.en: And they were all sitting there for about an hour processing these feelings with each other.
sentences.zh: 他们都在那里坐了一个小时，互相交流和消化这些情绪。

sentences.en: Then she remembered how her other brother had a falling out with his best friend when he was a preteen.
sentences.zh: 然后她想起她的另一个兄弟在青春期前夕是如何与他最好的朋友闹翻的。

sentences.en: I remember the enormous sadness of my brother around that sort of immediate, sort of dramatic departure of a friendship.
sentences.zh: 我记得我弟弟面对那种突如其来的、戏剧性的友谊破裂时感到的巨大悲伤。

sentences.en: All this started to change how Niobe listened.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切开始改变尼奥比倾听的方式。

sentences.en: I realized it was all around me that lots of boys, my brothers, my friends, my all sorts of boys and young men
sentences.zh: 我意识到它就发生在我身边，许多男孩、我的兄弟、我的朋友、各种各样的男孩和年轻男性

sentences.en: were talking about this desire or having these close friendships or desiring it.
sentences.zh: 都在谈论这种渴望，或者拥有这种亲密友谊，或者对它的渴望。

sentences.en: Niobe took these observations with her as she went on to get a PhD.
sentences.zh: 尼奥比带着这些观察结果去攻读博士学位。

sentences.en: She eventually became a developmental psychologist at NYU.
sentences.zh: 她最终成为了纽约大学的一名发展心理学家。

sentences.en: She's interviewed hundreds of boys since then, often circling back to the same kids year after year.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，她采访了数百名男孩，常常年复一年地回访同样的儿童。

sentences.en: The overwhelming majority have told her things like this, which she heard from a 15-year-old named Justin.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数人都对她说过这样的话，这是她从一个名叫贾斯廷的 15 岁男孩那里听到的。

sentences.en: We had teenage actors read the quotes.
sentences.zh: 我们请了青少年演员来朗读这些引言。

sentences.en: My best friend and I love each other.
sentences.zh: 我和我最好的朋友深爱着彼此。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: You have this thing that is so deep, it's within you.
sentences.zh: 你有这样一种东西，它是如此深沉，它就在你的内心。

sentences.en: You can't explain it.
sentences.zh: 你无法解释它。

sentences.en: It's just a thing that, you know, that that person is that person.
sentences.zh: 它只是一种你懂得的感觉，那个人就是那个人。

sentences.en: And that's all that should be important in our friendship.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在友谊中唯一应该看重的东西。

sentences.en: I guess in life, sometimes, two people can really, really understand each other
sentences.zh: 我想在生活中，有时两个人真的可以非常非常理解彼此，

sentences.en: and really have a trust, respect, and love for each other.
sentences.zh: 并且对彼此有真正的信任、尊重和爱。

sentences.en: It just happens.
sentences.zh: 它就是会发生。

sentences.en: It's like human nature.
sentences.zh: 这就像是人性。

sentences.en: She heard this about the importance of close friends from a 16-year-old.
sentences.zh: 她从一个 16 岁的男孩那里听到了关于亲密朋友重要性的看法。

sentences.en: I mean, if you just have your mother and your parents to talk to, then you're just going
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你只有母亲和父母可以倾诉，那么你就会把

sentences.en: to have all these ideas bottled up, and you're just going to go wacko because you can't express
sentences.zh: 所有这些想法都憋在心里，你最终会发疯的，因为你无法

sentences.en: yourself.
sentences.zh: 表达自己。

sentences.en: But as the boys got older, something happened.
sentences.zh: 但随着男孩们长大，事情发生了变化。

sentences.en: It became harder for them to express tenderness and vulnerability.
sentences.zh: 他们变得更难表达温柔和脆弱了。

sentences.en: Boys who had talked about how they loved their best friend or would go wacko without them
sentences.zh: 那些曾经谈论过他们多么爱自己的挚友，或者没有挚友就会发疯的男孩，

sentences.en: began to sound more like a stereotype of teenage boys, the ones who didn't want to have anything
sentences.zh: 开始听起来更像是对青少年男孩的刻板印象，也就是那些不想和

sentences.en: to do with touchy-feely stuff.
sentences.zh: 任何肉麻感伤的东西沾边的人。

sentences.en: Some of the boys go into sort of, I don't care, it doesn't matter, you know, whatever.
sentences.zh: 有些男孩会表现出一种“我不在乎，无所谓，随便吧”的态度。

sentences.en: But they say, I don't care so many times that you sense exactly that they do very much care.
sentences.zh: 但他们说了那么多遍“不在乎”，以至于你能真切地感觉到他们其实非常在乎。

sentences.en: Some of the older boys did talk to Niobe about the sadness they felt at disappearing
sentences.zh: 一些年龄较大的男孩确实向尼奥比谈到了他们对友谊消逝感到的悲伤。

sentences.en: friendships.
sentences.zh: 友谊。

sentences.en: A high school senior described how his friendships have changed since freshman year.
sentences.zh: 一名高中高年级学生描述了他的友谊自高一以来是如何改变的。

sentences.en: My friendship with my best friend is fading, but I'm saying it's still there.
sentences.zh: 我和我最好朋友的友谊正在褪色，但我得说它还在。

sentences.en: So I mean, it's still there because we still do stuff together, but only once in a while.
sentences.zh: 所以我的意思是它还在，因为我们还是一起做事，但只是偶尔。

sentences.en: It's sad because he lives only one block away from me, and I get to do stuff with him less
sentences.zh: 这很让人难过，因为他只住在我家隔壁一个街区，但我跟他一起做事的频率

sentences.en: than I get to do stuff for people who are way further.
sentences.zh: 甚至还不如那些住得很远的人。

sentences.en: So I'm like, it's like a DJ used his crossfader and started fading it slowly and slowly,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，这就像一个 DJ 使用了交叉推子，开始慢慢地把它淡出，

sentences.en: and now I'm like halfway through the crossfade.
sentences.zh: 现在我感觉已经进行到交叉淡出的中间了。

sentences.en: This is the language of boys.
sentences.zh: 这就是男孩的语言。

sentences.en: I mean, this is just, you know, remarkably beautiful language about talking about how
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直是，你知道的，非常美丽的语言，用来谈论

sentences.en: they're feeling and what's happening in the relational world around them.
sentences.zh: 他们的感受以及他们周围的关系世界中正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: So the idea is that boys aren't just being emotional.
sentences.zh: 所以这个观点是，男孩们不仅仅是在情绪化。

sentences.en: They're actually reading the world in a beautiful, you know, articulate way,
sentences.zh: 他们实际上在以一种美丽的、你知道的、清晰的方式解读这个世界，

sentences.en: which is exactly how they're stereotyped not to be able to do.
sentences.zh: 而这恰恰是刻板印象认为他们做不到的。

sentences.en: The stereotype that boys are less emotional than girls doesn't hold up when Niobe interviews boys.
sentences.zh: 当尼奥比采访男孩时，“男孩比女孩情绪少”的刻板印象根本站不住脚。

sentences.en: These are human beings with unbelievable emotional and social capacity,
sentences.zh: 这些是具有令人难以置信的情感和社会能力的人类，

sentences.en: and we as a culture just completely try to zip it out of them, and we ignore it.
sentences.zh: 而我们作为一个文化群体，却完全试图将这一点从他们身上抹杀掉，并且无视它。

sentences.en: Niobe has an explanation for why boys have trouble maintaining close bonds with one another.
sentences.zh: 尼奥比对为什么男孩难以维持彼此间的紧密联系给出了解释。

sentences.en: The reason for that struggle really is quite simple,
sentences.zh: 造成这种困境的原因其实非常简单，

sentences.en: which is that it's American masculinity and masculine norms and masculine expectations
sentences.zh: 那就是美国的男子气概、男性规范以及男性的期望，

sentences.en: that make, you know, close friendships into a girly gay thing rather than simply a human thing.
sentences.zh: 让亲密的友谊变成了某种娘娘腔的、同性恋般的事物，而不是单纯的人性使然。

sentences.en: So as boys grow older and enter manhood,
sentences.zh: 因此，随着男孩长大并步入成年，

sentences.en: they begin to be overwhelmed with this expectation that somehow they have to be, you know, on their own.
sentences.zh: 他们开始被这种期望压得喘不过气来，即不知为何他们必须，你知道的，靠自己。

sentences.en: They can't depend on others.
sentences.zh: 他们不能依赖他人。

sentences.en: They have to be fully independent.
sentences.zh: 他们必须完全独立。

sentences.en: That somehow the desire for intimacy with other boys is problematic in a culture that's very hyper-masculine.
sentences.zh: 在高度推崇男子气概的文化中，对与其他男孩建立亲密关系的渴望不知为何成了一个问题。

sentences.en: This hyper-masculinity, boys pick it up quickly and unconsciously.
